definition: An emergency call system is a home-based socio-technical setup designed to detect urgent events, especially falls or unusual inactivity, and quickly alert for help. In the described context, it can include a base station, wearable fall-detection sensors, home motion sensors, and access to social support services.

reasons: The definition claims detection of “unusual inactivity”; the packet describes emergency detection using motion sensors and a necklace with fall detection sensors, but does not mention inactivity detection as a feature.
The definition says the system “quickly alert[s] for help”; the packet mentions an emergency call system and support services, but does not explicitly state that alerts occur quickly.

Other elements (base station, home motion sensors, a wearable/necklace fall-detection sensor, and a social service) are supported by the packet, but the unsupported “unusual inactivity” and “quickly alert” components prevent a full pass.

The packet supports a home-based emergency call system with a base station, home motion sensors, a necklace with fall-detection sensors, and a social service, but it does not support the added claim that the system detects “unusual inactivity.”

“Quickly alert for help” is only indirectly supported by the description that fall sensors may trigger an emergency call automatically and that the system promises immediate responses; the definition should not extend beyond the packet’s wording.
